# railway_group (Resource)

A canvas group, as `railway.Group`. Put services, databases, volumes and buckets in it with their `group` attribute. Railway lists a group in the environment only while something belongs to it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "environment_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "railway_group" "data" {
  environment_id = var.environment_id
  name           = "data"
  color          = "#0f766e"
}

resource "railway_bucket" "backups" {
  environment_id = var.environment_id
  name           = "backups"
  group          = railway_group.data.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) ID of the Railway environment that holds this group. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `name` (String) Name of the group. Railway IaC addresses resources by name, so renaming replaces it.

### Optional

- `color` (String) Canvas color.
- `group` (String) Name of the parent group.
- `icon` (String) Canvas icon.
- `is_collapsed` (Boolean) Show the group collapsed on the canvas.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<environment_id>/<address>`, for example `c2b9…/group.web`.
- `live_changes` (List of String) Changes Railway needs to match this configuration, as `railway config plan` lists them. Empty after an apply; a refresh fills it when the live environment drifts, and the next plan applies them.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the Railway project the environment belongs to.
- `railway_id` (String) Railway's ID for this group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <environment_id>/group.<name>
terraform import railway_group.data 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/group.data
```
